reading-text-1.label: 阅读 Text 1
reading-text-1.title: 2017 考研英语二 阅读 Text 1

paragraphs.en: Every Saturday morning, at 9 am, more than 50,000 runners set off to run 5km around their local park. The Parkrun phenomenon began with a dozen friends and has inspired 400 events in the UK and more abroad. Events are free, staffed by thousands of volunteers. Runners range from four years old to grandparents; their times range from Andrew Baddeley’s world record 13 minutes 48 seconds up to an hour.
paragraphs.zh: 每个星期六早上9点，超过5万名跑步者出发，围绕当地公园跑5公里。Parkrun现象始于十几个朋友，在英国和国外激发了400场活动。活动是免费的，由数千名志愿者组成。跑步者从四岁到祖父母;他们的成绩从安德鲁·巴德利的世界纪录13分48秒到1小时不等。

paragraphs.en: Parkrun is succeeding where London’s Olympic “legacy” is failing. Ten years ago on Monday, it was announced that the Games of the 30th Olympiad would be in London. Planning documents pledged that the great legacy of the Games would be to lever a nation of sport lovers away from their couches. The population would be fitter, healthier and produce more winners. It has not happened. The number of adults doing weekly sport did rise, by nearly 2 million in the run-up to 2012—but the general population was growing faster. Worse, the numbers are now falling at an accelerating rate. The opposition claims primary school pupils doing at least two hours of sport a week have nearly halved. Obesity has risen among adults and children. Official retrospections continue as to why London 2012 failed to “inspire a generation.” The success of Parkrun offers answers. Parkun is not a race but a time trial: Your only competitor is the clock. The ethos welcomes anybody. There is as much joy over a puffed-out first-timer being clapped over the line as there is about top talent shining. The Olympic bidders, by contrast, wanted to get more people doing sports and to produce more elite athletes. The dual aim was mixed up: The stress on success over taking part was intimidating for newcomers.
paragraphs.zh: Parkrun在伦敦奥运“遗产”失败的地方取得了成功。10年前的周一，第30届奥运会宣布将在伦敦举行。规划文件承诺，奥运会的伟大遗产将是让一个体育爱好者的国家离开他们的沙发。人口将更加健康，更健康，产生更多的赢家。这并没有发生。每周参加体育运动的成年人数量确实增加了，在2012年之前增加了近200万--但总人口增长更快。更糟糕的是，目前，这一数字正在加速下降。反对派声称，每周至少运动两小时的小学生人数几乎减少了一半。成年人和儿童的肥胖人数都有所增加。官方仍在继续追溯2012年伦敦奥运会未能“激励一代人”的原因。Parkun的成功提供了答案。Parkun不是一场比赛，而是一场计时赛：你唯一的竞争对手是时钟。这里的风气欢迎任何人。一个气喘吁吁的第一次参赛者被鼓掌冲过终点线的喜悦，和顶尖人才闪耀的喜悦一样多。相比之下，奥运会申办者，想要让更多的人参加体育运动，同时培养更多的精英运动员。这两个目标是混淆的：对新人来说，成功的压力超过了参与的压力。

paragraphs.en: Indeed, there is something a little absurd in the state getting involved in the planning of such a fundamentally “grassroots” concept as community sports associations. If there is a role for government, it should really be getting involved in providing common goods—making sure there is space for playing fields and the money to pave tennis and netball courts, and encouraging the provision of all these activities in schools. But successive governments have presided over selling green spaces, squeezing money from local authorities and declining attention on sport in education. Instead of wordy, worthy strategies, future governments need to do more to provide the conditions for sport to thrive. Or at least not make them worse.
paragraphs.zh: 事实上，国家参与社区体育协会这样一个基本上“草根”概念的规划，有点荒谬。如果政府有作用的话，它真的应该参与提供公共物品--确保有运动场的空间和铺设网球场和无挡板篮球场的资金，并鼓励在学校提供所有这些活动。但历届政府都在出售绿色空间，从地方政府那里榨取资金，并减少对教育中体育的关注。而不是冗长，有价值的战略，未来的政府需要做更多的工作，为体育运动的蓬勃发展提供条件，或者至少不要让它们变得更糟。

reading-text-2.label: 阅读 Text 2
reading-text-2.title: 2017 考研英语二 阅读 Text 2

paragraphs.en: With so much focus on children’s use of screens, it’s easy for parents to forget about their own screen use. “Tech is designed to really suck you in,” says Jenny Radesky in her study of digital play, “and digital products are there to promote maximal engagement. It makes it hard to disengage, and leads to a lot of bleed-over into the family routine.”
paragraphs.zh: 由于太多的注意力集中在孩子们对屏幕的使用上，家长们很容易忘记他们自己对屏幕的使用。“技术的设计是为了真正吸引你，”珍妮·拉德斯基在她对数字游戏的研究中说，“数字产品的存在是为了促进最大的参与。它很难脱离，并导致家庭日常生活中的大量流血。”

paragraphs.en: Radesky has studied the use of mobile phones and tablets at mealtimes by giving mother-child pairs a food-testing exercise. She found that mothers who sued devices during the exercise started 20 percent fewer verbal and 39 percent fewer nonverbal interactions with their children. During a separate observation, she saw that phones became a source of tension in the family. Parents would be looking at their emails while the children would be making excited bids for their attention.
paragraphs.zh: Radesky研究了在用餐时间使用移动的手机和平板电脑的情况，她让母亲和孩子进行了一次食物测试。她发现，在测试过程中使用手机和平板电脑的母亲与孩子的语言互动减少了20%，非语言互动减少了39%。在另一项观察中，她发现手机成了家庭关系紧张的一个根源。父母在看他们的电子邮件，而孩子们则兴奋地吸引他们的注意力。

paragraphs.en: Infants are wired to look at parents’ faces to try to understand their world, and if those faces are blank and unresponsive—as they often are when absorbed in a device—it can be extremely disconcerting for the children. Radesky cites the “still face experiment” devised by developmental psychologist Ed Tronick in the 1970s. In it, a mother is asked to interact with her child in a normal way before putting on a blank expression and not giving them any visual social feedback: The child becomes increasingly distressed as she tries to capture her mother’s attention. “Parents don’t have to be exquisitely parents at all times, but there needs to be a balance and parents need to be responsive and sensitive to a child’s verbal or nonverbal expressions of an emotional need,” says Radesky. On the other hand, Tronick himself is concerned that the worries about kids’ use of screens are born out of an “oppressive ideology that demands that parents should always be interacting” with their children: “It’s based on a somewhat fantasized, very white, very upper-middle-class ideology that says if you’re failing to expose your child to 30,000 words you are neglecting them.” Tronick believes that just because a child isn’t learning from the screen doesn’t mean there’s no value to it—particularly if it gives parents time to have a shower, do housework or simply have a break from their child. Parents, he says, can get a lot out of using their devices to speak to a friend or get some work out of the way. This can make them feel happier, which lets them be more available to their child the rest of the time.
paragraphs.zh: 婴儿天生就喜欢看着父母的脸，试图理解他们的世界，如果父母的脸是空白的、没有反应的--当他们全神贯注于一个设备时，这对孩子来说是非常令人不安的。拉德斯基引用了发展心理学家艾德特罗尼克在20世纪70年代设计的“静止面孔实验”。在这个实验中，一位母亲被要求以正常的方式与她的孩子互动，然后摆出一副茫然的表情，不给他们任何视觉社会反馈：当孩子试图引起母亲的注意时，她变得越来越苦恼。“父母不必总是做一个精致的父母，但需要有一个平衡，父母需要对孩子的情感需求的语言或非语言表达做出反应和敏感，”Radesky说。另一方面，Tronick自己担心孩子使用屏幕的担忧是出于一种“压迫性的意识形态，要求父母应该总是与孩子互动”：“这是基于一种有点幻想的、非常白色、非常中上层阶级的意识形态，即如果你没有让你的孩子接触3万个单词，你就是在忽视它们。”特罗尼克认为，孩子没有从屏幕上学习并不意味着它没有价值--特别是如果它给父母洗澡的时间，做家务或只是和孩子分开休息。他说，父母可以从使用他们的设备与朋友交谈或完成一些工作中得到很多。这可以让他们感到更快乐，这让他们在剩下的时间里更容易接近孩子。

reading-text-3.label: 阅读 Text 3
reading-text-3.title: 2017 考研英语二 阅读 Text 3

paragraphs.en: Today, widespread social pressure to immediately go to college in conjunction with increasingly high expectations in a fast-moving world often causes students to completely overlook the possibility of taking a gap year. After all, if everyone you know is going to college in the fall, it seems silly to stay back a year, doesn’t it? And after going to school for 12 years, it doesn’t feel natural to spend a year doing something that isn’t academic.
paragraphs.zh: 如今，迅速发展的社会对学生普遍施加压力，要求他们立即上大学，再加上人们对他们的期望越来越高，这往往导致学生们完全忽视了休学一年的可能性。毕竟，如果你认识的每个人都要在秋季上大学，那么休学一年似乎很愚蠢，不是吗？在上学12年后，花一年时间做一些非学术性的事情感觉不太自然。

paragraphs.en: But while this may be true, it’s not a good enough reason to condemn gap years. There’s always a constant fear of falling behind everyone else on the socially perpetuated “race to the finish line,” whether that be toward graduate school, medical school or lucrative career. But despite common misconceptions, a gap year does not hinder the success of academic pursuits—in fact, it probably enhances it.
paragraphs.zh: 尽管这可能是真的，但这并不是谴责间隔年的充分理由。人们总是担心在社会上长期存在的“终点赛跑”中落后于其他人，无论是进入研究生院、医学院还是赚钱的职业。尽管存在普遍的误解，但间隔年并不会阻碍学业的成功--事实上，它可能会促进学业的成功。

paragraphs.en: Studies from the United States and Australia show that students who take a gap year are generally better prepared for and perform better in college than those who do not. Rather than pulling students back, a gap year pushes them ahead by preparing them for independence, new responsibilities and environmental changes—all things that first-year students often struggle with the most. Gap year experiences can lessen the blow when it comes to adjusting to college and being thrown into a brand new environment, making it easier to focus on academics and activities rather than acclimation blunders.
paragraphs.zh: 来自美国和澳大利亚的研究表明，与那些没有参加间隔年的学生相比，参加间隔年的学生通常会为上大学做更好的准备，在大学里的表现也会更好。间隔年不会让学生退缩，而是通过为独立做准备来推动他们前进，新的责任和环境的变化--所有这些首先--一年的学生往往最挣扎。间隔年的经验可以减轻打击，当谈到适应大学和被扔到一个全新的环境，这使得它更容易专注于学术和活动，而不是适应错误。

paragraphs.en: If you’re not convinced of the inherent value in taking a year off to explore interests, then consider its financial impact on future academic choices. According to the National Center for Education Statistics, nearly 80 percent of college students end up changing their majors at least once. This isn’t surprising, considering the basic mandatory high school curriculum leaves students with a poor understanding of the vast academic possibilities that await them in college. Many students find themselves listing one major on their college applications, but switching to another after taking college classes. It’s not necessarily a bad thing, but depending on the school, it can be costly to make up credits after switching too late in the game. At Boston College, for example, you would have to complete an extra year were you to switch to the nursing school from another department. Taking a gap year to figure things out initially can help prevent stress and save money later on.
paragraphs.zh: 如果你不相信花一年时间去探索兴趣的内在价值，那么考虑一下它对未来学术选择的经济影响。根据国家教育统计中心的数据，近80%的大学生最终至少换了一次专业。这并不奇怪，考虑到基本的强制性高中课程让学生对大学里等待他们的广阔的学术可能性知之甚少。许多学生发现，他们自己在大学申请表上列出了一个专业，但在上完大学课程后又换了另一个专业。这不一定是件坏事，但根据学校的不同，在太晚换专业后补学分可能会很昂贵。例如，在波士顿学院，如果你从其他部门转到护士学校，你必须完成额外的一年。用一个间隔年来解决最初的问题可以帮助你避免压力以后还能省钱

reading-text-4.label: 阅读 Text 4
reading-text-4.title: 2017 考研英语二 阅读 Text 4

paragraphs.en: Though often viewed as a problem for western states, the growing frequency of wildfires is a national concern because of its impact on federal tax dollars, says Professor Max Moritz, a specialist in fire ecology and management. In 2015, the US Forest Service for the first time spent more than half of its $5.5 billion annual budget fighting fires—nearly double the percentage it spent on such efforts 20 years ago. In effect, fewer federal funds today are going towards the agency’s other work—such as forest conservation, watershed and cultural resources management, and infrastructure upkeep—that affect the lives of all Americans.
paragraphs.zh: 火灾生态学和管理专家马克斯·莫里茨教授说，尽管野火的发生频率越来越高，但它对联邦税收的影响是一个全国性的问题。2015年，美国林务局首次将其55亿美元年度预算的一半以上用于灭火，实际上，如今用于该机构其他工作的联邦资金越来越少，如森林保护、流域和文化资源管理，以及基础设施维护，这些都影响到所有美国人的生活。

paragraphs.en: Another nationwide concern is whether public funds from other agencies are going into construction in fire-prone districts. As Moritz puts it, how often are federal dollars building homes that are likely to be lost to a wildfire? “It’s already a huge problem from a public expenditure perspective for the whole country,” he says. “We need to take a magnifying glass to that. Like, ‘Wait a minute, is this OK?’ Do we want instead to redirect those funds to concentrate on lower-hazard parts of the landscape?”
paragraphs.zh: 另一个全国性的担忧是，来自其他机构的公共资金是否被用于火灾多发区的建设。正如莫里茨所说，联邦资金用于建造可能在野火中被毁的房屋的频率有多高？“从公共支出的角度来看，这对整个国家来说已经是一个巨大的问题，”他说，“我们需要拿一个放大镜来看待这个问题。比如，'等一下，这样可以吗？我们是否希望将这些资金重新定向，集中在风险较低的地区？

paragraphs.en: Such a view would require a corresponding shift in the way US society today views fire, researchers say.
paragraphs.zh: 研究人员说，这种观点需要美国社会对火灾的看法发生相应的转变。

paragraphs.en: For one thing, conversations about wildfires need to be more inclusive. Over the past decade, the focus has been on climate change—how the warming of the Earth from greenhouse gases is leading to conditions that worsen fires. While climate is a key element, Moritz says, it shouldn’t come at the expense of the rest of the equation.
paragraphs.zh: 首先，关于野火的讨论需要更具包容性。在过去的十年里，焦点一直集中在气候变化上--温室气体导致地球变暖是如何导致火灾恶化的。莫里茨说，虽然气候是一个关键因素，但它不应该以牺牲其他因素为代价。

paragraphs.en: “The human systems and the landscapes we live on are linked, and the interactions go both ways,” he says. Failing to recognize that, he notes, leads to “an overly simplified view of what the solutions might be. Our perception of the problem and of what the solution is becomes very limited.” At the same time, people continue to treat fire as an event that needs to be wholly controlled and unleashed only out of necessity, says Professor Balch at the University of Colorado. But acknowledging fire’s inevitable presence in human life is an attitude crucial to developing the laws, policies, and practices that make it as safe as possible, she says.
paragraphs.zh: 他说：“人类系统和我们生活的环境是相互联系的，相互作用是双向的。”他指出，如果没有认识到这一点，就会导致“对解决方案的看法过于简单化。我们对问题和解决方案的看法变得非常有限。”与此同时，人们继续把火视为一种需要完全控制和释放的事件，科罗拉多大学的鲍尔奇教授说，但是承认火在人类生活中不可避免的存在是一种态度，这对制定法律、政策和实践，使其尽可能安全，她说。

paragraphs.en: “We’ve disconnected ourselves from living with fire,” Balch says. “It is really important to understand and try and tease out what is the human connection with fire today.”
paragraphs.zh: “我们已经脱离了与火的生活，”鲍尔奇说，“理解并尝试梳理出当今人类与火的联系是非常重要的。”
